summary:
FLARE AI is an agentic AI research assistant designed to support scientific research on fire behavior and combustion in microgravity. It uses a multi-agent architecture in which specialized AI agents collaborate to investigate NASA experiments, explore scientific datasets, analyze experimental results, and generate evidence-based research reports.

The platform integrates research from investigations such as SAFFIRE, BASS-II, and FLEX, helping users discover relevant publications, examine combustion parameters, compare experimental conditions, and visualize findings through interactive charts. Each agent contributes to a coordinated research workflow, transforming complex scientific information into structured and accessible insights.

FLARE AI addresses the challenge by making microgravity combustion data easier to explore, understand, and analyze. This is important because understanding how flames behave in space can support scientific progress and contribute to future spacecraft fire-safety research. FLARE AI aims to make this knowledge more accessible while maintaining scientific traceability through references and source-based findings.
details:
FLARE AI – Project Details

What does it do and how does it work?

FLARE AI is an Agentic AI Research Assistant designed to help researchers investigate fire behavior and combustion phenomena in microgravity. Rather than functioning as a traditional chatbot, it uses a coordinated multi-agent architecture in which specialized agents collaborate to complete scientific research tasks.

The platform is built around four specialized agents:

  • Research Agent: Discovers relevant NASA investigations, scientific publications and research references.
  • Data Agent: Retrieves, explores and organizes experimental datasets, including SAFFIRE, BASS-II and LUCI.
  • Scientific Analysis Agent: Examines experimental parameters, compares results and identifies patterns while respecting differences in experimental conditions.
  • Report Agent: Produces structured scientific summaries and reports supported by references and available evidence.

An orchestrator coordinates these agents according to the researcher's question. Users can interact through a conversational workspace, explore datasets, visualize results and access generated reports.

What benefits does it provide?

FLARE AI brings scientific research resources together in one accessible environment. It reduces the effort required to locate relevant experiments, navigate complex datasets and compare scientific findings. It also makes research workflows more transparent by connecting generated insights to their underlying sources.

What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make microgravity combustion research more accessible, understandable and efficient. By helping researchers investigate how flames behave under different experimental conditions, FLARE AI can support scientific exploration and contribute to research relevant to spacecraft fire safety and future space missions.

It is designed as a research-support tool, not an autonomous fire-prediction or certified safety system.

What technologies did we use?

Our development combines:

  • Python: Data processing, research workflows and AI agent implementation.
  • Pandas: Dataset exploration, cleaning and analysis.
  • NASA research resources: Scientific investigations, publications and experimental data.
  • FastAPI: Backend services and API integration.
  • Next.js, React and TypeScript: Interactive frontend and research workspace.
  • Multi-agent AI architecture: Coordination of specialized research, data, analysis and reporting agents.
  • Data visualization libraries: Presentation of experimental results and comparisons.

How is the project creative and innovative?

The main innovation is applying agentic AI to scientific research rather than limiting AI to question answering. FLARE AI transforms a research question into a coordinated workflow: discovering sources, exploring datasets, analyzing experimental evidence and generating a structured report.

Instead of relying on a single general-purpose AI response, specialized agents contribute different capabilities. This approach makes the research process more organized, traceable and useful for scientific exploration.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered scientific accuracy, data provenance, experimental comparability and transparency. Different investigations may use different materials, measurement units, pressure levels, oxygen concentrations and gravity conditions. Therefore, the platform must preserve original measurements, identify missing information and distinguish microgravity experiments from simulated lunar-gravity experiments.

We also prioritized modular architecture, usability and clear presentation of scientific evidence, ensuring that the platform can be extended with additional investigations and datasets in the future.
